title: Thorn's Spotlight matches a missing child's NCMEC photo to online sex ads; she may have been recovered within weeks
summary: In April 2019 a California officer ran a NCMEC missing-child photo through Thorn's Spotlight; Rekognition matching returned sex ads with the girl and, per Thorn's CEO, she was recovered within weeks.
account: The source places the case in April 2019 without a day. Thorn CEO Julie Cordua, speaking at an Amazon conference, was quoted by WIRED's Tom Simonite. She said a California law enforcement officer screenshotted a missing child's picture from a National Center for Missing and Exploited Children post. The officer ran it through Spotlight, Thorn's investigator tool that matches faces and other clues in online sex ads. Using Amazon's facial recognition, Spotlight returned a list of ads featuring the girl, who had been sold for weeks. More traditional police work followed and, she said, the child was recovered within weeks. Snopes notes Thorn's 2017 impact report claimed its tools helped identify 5,791 child victims and rescue 103. The figures are from Thorn's surveys of police users, and viral claims conflated identification with rescue. No police or court record of this case is among the sources.
purpose: Help law-enforcement investigators find underage sex-trafficking victims by matching faces and text across online escort advertisements.
developer: Thorn (with Amazon Rekognition for face matching)
deployer: An unnamed California law enforcement officer and agency
taxonomy_note: The recovery is reported only by the maker's CEO, and the AI's documented part was returning the ads.

ratings.reason: A child sold for weeks was recovered and removed from trauma, per Thorn's CEO. No independent confirmation of the recovery is among the sources.

ai_role.statement: The face match that surfaced the ads is attributed to Amazon Rekognition inside Spotlight. The recovery itself came from conventional police work. Everything about this case rests on Thorn's CEO. Snopes documents that Thorn's aggregate figures derive from user surveys and were widely misreported.

evidence.title: How Facial Recognition Is Fighting Child Sex Trafficking
evidence.quote: Using Amazon’s facial recognition technology, Spotlight quickly returned a list of online sex ads featuring the girl’s photo.

evidence.citation: Dan MacGuill, Snopes fact check, 4 Sep 2018
evidence.title: Did Ashton Kutcher's Software Help Rescue 6,000 Children from Sex Trafficking?
evidence.quote: As stated by Thorn themselves, the organization's digital tools had helped identify -- not rescue -- almost 6,000 child victims, a distinction that has sometimes been overlooked.
